paragraph_text: (B8) (P. Dehornoy) We call a braid word  w   \sigma-positive (resp.  \sigma-negative) if the generator  \sigma_i  with minimal index occurs only with  positive (resp.  negative) exponents  in  w.   Is it true that, for every  n,  there exists a constant  c(n)  such that every  n-strand braid word of length  N  is equivalent to a  \sigma-positive or a  \sigma-negative braid word of length  c(n) N  at most ?
